title: The `main` branch has no branch protection and no ruleset, so not one CI job is a required check and every ci.yml comment claiming a step blocks merges is false
description: I queried the public GitHub API for this repository. `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/branches/main` returns `protected: false` with `protection.required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"` and empty `contexts` and `checks` arrays; `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/rules/branches/main` returns an empty array, so no repository ruleset applies either. ci.yml runs five jobs on `pull_request: branches: [main]` (lint, typecheck, test, extension, build) and its comments assert they gate merges: line 43 "format drift should block merges", lines 65-66 "removed `continue-on-error: true`. Typecheck must block merges", line 70 "block merges on high/critical CVEs in runtime deps". None of these are required checks, so a red CI run is advisory only and the merge button stays green. The same absence means .github/CODEOWNERS is decorative: CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers but only enforces review when "Require review from Code Owners" is set in branch protection, and it is not. Direct pushes to main are also unrestricted.
impact: The entire CI investment (SHA-pinned actions, a Prettier gate, a hard typecheck, an `npm audit` gate on 71 runtime dependencies, an extension build, a Next.js build) enforces nothing. Broken TypeScript, a failing test suite, or a high-severity CVE in a production dependency can be merged or pushed straight to main with a single click, and the next `v*` tag turns that into a published image and a GitHub release. It also means the two-person review flow the CODEOWNERS file describes is not actually required for lib/auth, lib/billing, or .github.
recommendation: Add a ruleset (or classic branch protection) on `main` that requires the Lint, Typecheck, Test, Extension, and Build check names, requires at least one approving review, requires review from code owners, and blocks force pushes and direct pushes. Commit the ruleset JSON under .github/ so the configuration is reviewable in-repo rather than living only in the web UI.

title: Dependabot auto-merge calls `gh pr merge --auto` into an unprotected main, so with zero required checks a dependency bump merges the instant it opens, before CI has run
description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:32 runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash "$PR_URL"` for any dependabot PR whose `update-type` is `version-update:semver-patch` (line 30) and which lacks the `dependabot-merge-ignore` label. The workflow header at line 3 states the guarantee: "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes." `--auto` does not wait for CI; it waits for the PR to become mergeable under the branch's protection rules. Per ci-02, `main` has `protected: false`, `required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`, empty `contexts`, and no ruleset, so a dependabot PR is mergeable at the moment it opens and auto-merge fires immediately, with lint, typecheck, test and build still queued or running. The workflow grants itself `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` at lines 11-13. Separately, ci.yml's `npm ci` steps (lines 37, 62, 101, 138, 193) run with no `--ignore-scripts` and .npmrc contains only `audit-level=high`, `fund=false`, `update-notifier=false`, so package lifecycle scripts execute in CI. (If the repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting happens to be off, `gh pr merge --auto` errors instead and the entire workflow is dead on every dependabot PR; that is the alternative reading and is also a finding.)
impact: A compromised patch release of any of the 71 runtime dependencies is merged to main with no human review and without a single CI job having passed, and its install scripts then run in every subsequent CI job. The next `v*` tag builds that main into the published GHCR image and the signed release tarball, so the compromise propagates to every self-hosted install through the in-app updater. The `npm audit --audit-level=high` gate at ci.yml:71 only catches advisories that already exist, which by definition a fresh malicious release does not have. The stated safety property ("after CI passes") is not enforced anywhere in the repository.
recommendation: Fix ci-02 first: `--auto` is only meaningful once required status checks exist. Then either require Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build as checks on main, or replace `--auto` with an explicit gate in this workflow (a `needs:` on a job that re-runs the suite, or `gh pr checks --watch` before merging). Also restrict auto-merge to devDependencies, or add a cooldown so a package released in the last N days is never auto-merged.

title: The browser extension's 194-package dependency tree has no security monitoring at all: Dependabot only watches `/`, and the extension CI job never runs npm audit
category: no dependency monitoring on a shipped artifact
description: `.github/dependabot.yml` declares exactly two update configs, both scoped to the repo root: `package-ecosystem: "npm"` with `directory: "/"` (line 5) and `package-ecosystem: "github-actions"` with `directory: "/"` (line 84). Dependabot directories are not recursive, so `extension/package.json` and `extension/package-lock.json` (194 lockfile entries, of which 191 are dev) are never scanned and never produce a PR. The CI side has the same hole: the only audit step in the repo is `.github/workflows/ci.yml:71`, `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`, which runs in the `typecheck` job with the default working directory (repo root) and with `--omit=dev`. The separate `extension` job at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:115` runs `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, and `npm run build:chrome && npm run build:firefox` (lines 136 to 150) and has no audit step. The SBOM is generated by `anchore/sbom-action` against the built Docker image (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:82`), which contains the Next.js app and not the extension, so the extension zips attached to the release at `.github/workflows/release.yml:147` ship with no SBOM either. `--omit=dev` matters here specifically: the extension has only 2 runtime dependencies and 191 dev packages, and those dev packages (vite, rollup, esbuild, sharp, archiver) are the entire toolchain that produces `content.js`, the IIFE injected into every page the user visits via `content_scripts.matches: ["<all_urls>"]` (`extension/manifest/chrome.json:47`). A compromised build dependency writes straight into a browser-privileged artifact distributed through the Chrome Web Store and AMO. `npm audit --json` in `extension/` reports 0 vulnerabilities today, so nothing is currently exploitable; the finding is that nothing in the repo would tell anyone when that changes.
impact: A published CVE in any of the extension's 194 packages, including the build chain that emits the all-URLs content script, produces no Dependabot PR and no CI failure. The maintainer finds out only by manually running npm audit inside extension/, which nothing prompts them to do. For an extension already installed in users' browsers, the window between disclosure and a store update is unbounded.
recommendation: Add a third Dependabot config block with `package-ecosystem: "npm"` and `directory: "/extension"` (same schedule and labels as the root block), and add an `- name: Audit extension dependencies` / `run: npm audit --audit-level=high` step with `working-directory: extension` to the `extension` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` after the `npm ci` step at line 138. Do not pass `--omit=dev` there: for the extension the dev tree is the shipped tree.

title: DISABLE_CSP=1 was shipped in production env
description: Operator-set env var stripped every security header (CSP, COOP, CORP, XFO, Permissions-Policy, HSTS) silently.
recommendation: env validator refuses DISABLE_CSP=1 when NODE_ENV=production. Removed from .env.local.

title: Docker base + compose tag both mutable
description: node:22-alpine and ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:latest are moving targets; a compromised registry push immediately ships to every self-hoster.
recommendation: Pinned to node:22.11.0-alpine (self-hosters can replace with @sha256:<digest>). Compose uses :3.0.0. Added tini for PID 1 signal forwarding + HEALTHCHECK.

title: Half of .github/labeler.yml uses an invented schema the labeler action silently ignores, so the step named "Apply size label" has never applied a size label
description: actions/labeler takes the label name as the top-level key and accepts only `changed-files`, `base-branch`, `head-branch`, `any` and `all` as matcher keys. .github/labeler.yml gets this right for four blocks (`ci` line 24, `config` line 29, `security` line 35, `docs` line 39) and wrong for the other two. The `size` block (lines 3-16) has a top-level key `size` whose entries are `{label: "size/xs", files: [...]}`, and the `dependencies` block (lines 18-21) uses `{label: "dependencies", from-branch: [...]}`. `label`, `files` and `from-branch` are not matcher keys. I confirmed against the action's source (src/api/get-label-configs.ts): an unrecognised key is not an error, it hits `core.info(\`An unknown config option was under ${label}: ${key}\`)` and produces no matcher, so the labels `size`, `size/xs`, `size/s`, `size/m`, `size/l` and the branch-based `dependencies` rule are never applied. The step at .github/workflows/label.yml:16 is literally named "Apply size label". Separately, label.yml:7-8 declares `permissions: pull-requests: write` only; declaring any permission sets every unlisted scope to `none`, including `contents`, while the action's documented usage requires `contents: read` to read the configuration file from the repository.
impact: PR triage silently does not work. Maintainers see no size labels, and the `dependencies` label the stale.yml exemption logic and the auto-merge ignore flow both reason about is never applied from the branch name (dependabot supplies it from .github/dependabot.yml:12-14 instead, which masks the breakage). Nothing in the log makes this visible except an `info`-level line nobody reads.
recommendation: Rewrite the `size` and `dependencies` blocks in .github/labeler.yml to the real schema: one top-level key per label (`size/xs:`, `size/s:`, ...) with `- changed-files: - any-glob-to-any-file: [...]`, and `dependencies: - head-branch: ["^dependabot/"]`. Note that labeler matches on paths, not diff size, so if a real size label is wanted use a line-count action instead. Add `contents: read` to the permissions block in .github/workflows/label.yml:7.

title: The GitHub Action gate stops at severity counts and never uploads the SARIF the API already produces, so findings never reach the Security tab that ZAP, Nuclei and Snyk actions all populate
description: The composite action at .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml is complete and correct: it starts a scan, polls GET /scan/status, and at :152 to :176 reads only summary.critical/high/medium/low/total, writes a step summary table, and exits 1 on threshold breach. It never fetches SARIF. A full SARIF 2.1.0 generator already exists at lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 and is exposed as GET /api/v3/history/[id]/report?format=sarif (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:174), and app/docs/reports/page.tsx:310 to :319 already publishes the exact two-step recipe (curl the SARIF, then github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3) as something the user must hand-assemble. The action already emits scan-id as an output (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:45), so the two halves are one curl apart. Separately, the action lives at .github/actions/scan-gate/ inside the app repo, which is not a GitHub Marketplace-publishable location: Marketplace requires action.yml at the root of its own repository plus a tagged release. ZAP ships official Marketplace actions, Nuclei ships one, and Snyk and Burp both list Actions integrations (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors.md, ZAP and Nuclei sections).
impact: A developer wiring VulnRadar into CI gets a red X and a markdown table, while the equivalent ZAP or Nuclei action gets them annotated Code Scanning alerts inline on the pull-request diff, with dismissal and tracking handled by GitHub. That is the difference between a gate people keep and a gate people delete after the second false alarm. And because the action is not on the Marketplace, the highest-intent discovery channel for this product (a developer searching the Actions marketplace for "security scan") returns nothing.
recommendation: Two changes, both small. First, in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml add an optional `sarif-file` input (default `vulnradar.sarif`); after the poll loop succeeds, curl `$VR_API_BASE/history/$scan_id/report?format=sarif` to that path and add a `sarif-file` output, then document the follow-on `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` step in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299's snippet so the published example is the complete one. Second, mirror the action into a dedicated `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action` repo with action.yml at the root and a v1 tag, publish it to the Marketplace, and change the `uses:` in app/docs/api/page.tsx:1299 from the current `${APP_REPO}/.github/actions/scan-gate@main` (an unpinned branch reference) to `VulnRadar/scan-gate-action@v1`.

title: API_VERSION exists so "all API calls" can be switched between versions, but 60 fetch call sites across 28 files hardcode the /api/v3 path instead
description: lib/config/client-constants.ts:80-83 declares `// API VERSION - Change this to switch all API calls between versions` followed by `export const API_VERSION = "v3"`, and :87 onwards builds the whole API route map from it as template literals. That map is used correctly 157 times across app/ and components/. It is also bypassed 60 times in 28 files by fetches that spell the version out: app/admin/page.tsx alone has five (:350, :447, :456, :468, :489), plus app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:73, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx:35, app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:34, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx:36, app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:55, app/dashboard/page.tsx:273 and app/unsubscribe/page.tsx:197 among others. lib/config/config-values.ts:659-660 additionally exports CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION and CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS as a second, unconnected copy of the same fact.
impact: The stated purpose of the constant is not achievable: bumping API_VERSION to v4 leaves 60 client calls pointed at v3, so the app would half-migrate with no compile error and no test failure, and the breakage would surface as scattered 404s in admin, checkout, dashboard and unsubscribe. This is the reverse-check shape the section is about: the operator or maintainer believes they changed one value and changed 72 percent of the call sites. Not self-host-breaking today, since v3 is the only supported version, but it makes the one migration the constant exists for unsafe.
recommendation: Add the missing routes to the API map in lib/config/client-constants.ts:87 onwards (admin teams, admin updater status, ai conversations, ai info, auth me is already there, account unsubscribe) and replace the 60 literals with the map entries. Then add an ESLint `no-restricted-syntax` rule scoped to app/ and components/ that flags any string literal matching `/api/v\d`, so the 61st cannot be added silently. Also collapse CONFIG_API_CURRENT_VERSION into API_VERSION so there is one source of truth rather than two.

title: Coverage measures only .ts, so 419 React files and 95,294 lines are invisible, and with environment:node and no jsdom the suite cannot render a component even if someone wrote a test
category: whole layer outside the test harness
description: coverage.include is ["lib/**/*.ts", "app/**/*.ts"] (vitest.config.ts:31). The glob `*.ts` does not match `.tsx`. The coverage run confirms it: exactly 412 files are measured, which is 250 lib/*.ts plus 162 app/*.ts, and not one .tsx. Unmeasured: 266 components/*.tsx plus 47 components/*.ts (313 files, 65,147 lines), 152 app/*.tsx (30,147 lines), and 1 lib/*.tsx. Separately, test.environment is "node" (line 23) and package.json lists no jsdom, no happy-dom, and no @testing-library/* in either dependencies or devDependencies, so no test can mount a React tree at all. The eight files under tests/components/ cover 8 of 313 component files (2.6%), and six of those eight targets are plain .ts utility modules (queue-status-utils.ts, settings-registry-utils.ts, use-unsaved-changes-warning.ts, admin/utils.ts, schedule-time-utils.ts, ai-review-gate.ts); only danger-score-trend.tsx and auth-provider.tsx are .tsx, and those tests can reach only their non-rendering exports.
impact: Every form-validation rule, every conditional that hides a paid feature behind a plan check, every auth-state branch in a client component, and every result renderer is untested and unmeasured. A regression that shows a Pro-only control to a free user, or that renders a scan as clean when findings exist, reaches production with a green CI. The measurement gap makes it worse than it looks: the 81.02% headline reads as broad health while a third of the app's lines are simply not in the denominator.
recommendation: Two steps, and the first is cheap. Change coverage.include to ["lib/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "app/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "components/**/*.{ts,tsx}", "middleware.ts"] so the real denominator is visible even before any test is written; expect the headline to drop, which is the accurate number. Then add jsdom plus @testing-library/react as devDependencies and an environmentMatchGlobs entry mapping tests/components/** to jsdom, and start with the highest-risk components: components/scanner/scan-form.tsx, the plan-gated controls, and the shared ScanResultDetail renderer.

title: middleware.ts, the 546-line request gate for every route in the app, sits outside coverage.include so its 365-line test suite produces no measurable coverage
description: middleware.ts is 546 lines and lives at the repo root, so it matches neither "lib/**/*.ts" nor "app/**/*.ts" in coverage.include (vitest.config.ts:31). It does not appear in the coverage-summary.json I generated: filtering the 412 measured files for 'middleware' returns nothing. tests/middleware.test.ts exists and is 365 lines, so the file is not untested, but there is no way to tell which of its branches the suite reaches. This matters because middleware is where the public-path allowlist and the auth redirect live, and AUDIT-012 filed three separate HIGH findings against that allowlist (authz-01, authz-02, authz-03: the public host report API, all three staff-oidc endpoints, and the public contact form all missing from PUBLIC_PATHS, each breaking the feature for logged-out visitors). lib/config/public-paths.ts reports 100% statements but only 1 statement, because it is a data table: line coverage says nothing about whether the table is correct. instrumentation.ts is excluded outright (vitest.config.ts:38) and is 3,639 lines holding 72 CREATE TABLE and 97 CREATE INDEX statements.
impact: The single file that decides whether a request is authenticated, redirected, or allowed through unauthenticated has an unknown tested fraction. A branch added to it, for example a new public path or a new bypass condition, is invisible to both the coverage report and to a reviewer asking 'is this covered?'. The AUDIT-012 authz findings show the concrete cost: three features silently broken for every logged-out visitor and crawler, shipped past a green suite.
recommendation: Add "middleware.ts" to coverage.include in vitest.config.ts so the file is measured, then read the resulting branch percentage and fill the gaps in tests/middleware.test.ts. Separately, add a table-driven test that walks every entry in PUBLIC_PATHS and asserts each named route file actually exists, and walks every route.ts the app serves unauthenticated and asserts it is listed, which is the drift the three AUDIT-012 authz findings all were.

title: Severity ordering is redeclared in nine private tables under three mutually incompatible numeric conventions, two of which share the identifier SEVERITY_RANK, and the info label already differs between the app and the ~750 public /checks pages
description:
There is a canonical severity ordering: SEVERITY_PRIORITY at lib/config/constants.ts:628 (critical 5, high 4, medium 3, low 2, info 1), consumed with a `b - a` comparator by components/scanner/results-list.tsx:335, app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:236, app/api/v3/scan/bulk/route.ts:252 and app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:427. Eight further private tables encode the same idea:

Convention A, critical is 5 down to info is 1 (same as canonical): lib/scanner/dedupe.ts:18 `SEVERITY_RANK`, lib/reports/compliance-report.ts:37 `SEVERITY_RANK`.
Convention B, critical is 0 up to info is 4 (inverted): lib/ai/scan-summary.ts:47 `SEVERITY_RANK`, lib/ai/auto-tag-suggest.ts:136 `SEVERITY_RANK`, lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:78 `SEVERITY_ORDER`, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:73 `SEVERITY_ORDER`.
Convention C, info is 0 up to critical is 4 (a third numbering): lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts:715 `SEVERITY_RANK`.

So the identifier `SEVERITY_RANK` means three different things in five files, and the comparator direction flips with it: compliance-report.ts:150 sorts `severityRank(b) - severityRank(a)` while scan-summary.ts:77 and auto-tag-suggest.ts:166 sort `severityRank(a) - severityRank(b)`, and both are correct only for their own table. Lifting either constant into a shared module, or copying a comparator between these files, silently reverses the ordering with no type error, because every table is `Record<Severity, number>`.

The name `SEVERITY_ORDER` is separately overloaded: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:12 exports it as `readonly Severity[]` (consumed by six other components: results-list.tsx:345, dashboard.tsx:428, ai-choice-modal.tsx:154, ai-verify-result-modal.tsx:60, repos/page.tsx:49 and github-scan-result-modal.tsx:59), lib/reports/markdown-report.ts:23 declares another `Severity[]`, and execute-scan.ts:78 / execute-crawl-scan.ts:73 declare it as a numeric Record.

The label layer has already drifted user-visibly. components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:71 (SEVERITY_TONE), lib/reports/markdown-report.ts:31 and lib/reports/compliance-report.ts:29 all label the lowest level "Info". lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:25 labels it "Informational", and that is the SeverityPill rendered on app/checks/[id]/page.tsx and app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx, which is the ~750-page public SEO surface. There are also two different components exported as `SeverityPill` (components/history/severity-pill.tsx:11, which delegates to severityTone(), and lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:41, which inlines its own hsl alphas of 0.1/0.25 against SEVERITY_TONE's /15 and /40), plus four colour maps: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx SEVERITY_TONE, components/docs/docs-types.ts:75 SEVERITY_COLORS, lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:18 SEVERITY_COLORS as RGB tuples, and lib/config/client-constants.ts:304 SEVERITY_COLORS, which has zero consumers.
impact: Today: the same info-severity finding reads "Info" in the product and "Informational" on the public check pages, and the same severity pill has two different tints depending on which surface renders it. Tomorrow: a developer who consolidates `SEVERITY_RANK` (a natural cleanup, since the name is already shared) or copies a working comparator between two of these files inverts a sort with no compile error, and findings list least-severe-first in a report, an AI summary, or the dedupe winner selection. lib/scanner/dedupe.ts:175 uses its rank to pick which duplicate finding survives, so an inversion there would keep the info-level copy and discard the critical one.
recommendation: Put one table in lib/config/client-constants.ts next to SEVERITY_LEVELS: keep SEVERITY_PRIORITY's convention (critical highest) and export both it and the ordered array. Delete the seven private tables and rewrite each comparator to `PRIORITY[b.severity] - PRIORITY[a.severity]`, checking each one's direction as you go (lib/ai/scan-summary.ts:77, lib/ai/auto-tag-suggest.ts:166, lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:712, lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:220 and :585 all currently sort ascending against an inverted table). Rename lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:78 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:73 out of the way first so `SEVERITY_ORDER` unambiguously means the array. Move SEVERITY_TONE's labels to that same module and have lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:25 read them so "Info" is one string, and delete the unconsumed lib/config/client-constants.ts:304 SEVERITY_COLORS.

title: 2FA pending-challenge window is admin-editable but the login route still uses the compiled constant
description: 2FA_PENDING_MAX_AGE_SECONDS has no getSetting consumer anywhere. app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts still imports and uses the compiled AUTH_2FA_PENDING_MAX_AGE constant to set the pending-2FA cookie's maxAge -- an admin changing this window in the panel has no effect on actual cookie lifetime.
recommendation: Replace the AUTH_2FA_PENDING_MAX_AGE import in login/route.ts with getSetting("2FA_PENDING_MAX_AGE_SECONDS") where the cookie is set.

title: docker-compose postgres uses mutable postgres:16-alpine tag
description: Postgres image is on a moving tag, not pinned to a specific minor or digest. A poisoned upstream push silently propagates.
recommendation: Pin to postgres:16.4-alpine or @sha256:<digest>.

title: The SBOM covers only the Docker image, so the two browser-extension zips attached to the same release ship with no bill of materials at all
description: docker-publish.yml:82-91 runs `anchore/sbom-action` with `image: ghcr.io/.../vulnradar:${{ github.ref_name }}`, so the CycloneDX SBOM describes only what is inside the server image. release.yml:117-148 separately builds the browser extension (`npm ci`, `build:chrome`, `build:firefox`) and attaches `vulnradar-chrome-vX.Y.Z.zip` and `vulnradar-firefox-vX.Y.Z.zip` to the same GitHub release; I confirmed against the live releases API that v3.6.0 through v3.7.2 each carry both zips plus one `.sbom.cdx.json`. The extension is a separate package with its own lockfile (194 packages per AUDIT-013#subdeps-02) and none of it appears in the image, so none of it appears in the SBOM. SECURITY.md:82-83 describes the SBOM as a "full software bill of materials" for the release without qualifying that it excludes the extension.
impact: A downstream consumer running SBOM-based vulnerability scanning against the release believes they have covered everything VulnRadar ships. They have not covered the two artifacts that execute in an end user's browser with host permissions, and those are also the artifacts with no Dependabot monitoring (AUDIT-013#subdeps-02).
recommendation: Add a second `anchore/sbom-action` invocation in release.yml after the extension build, pointed at `${RUNNER_TEMP}/extension-src/extension` with `path:` instead of `image:`, and attach it as `vulnradar-extension-vX.Y.Z.sbom.cdx.json`. Amend SECURITY.md:82 to name what each SBOM covers.

title: release.yml swallows a failed SBOM download with continue-on-error and passes an empty run-id on the manual-publish path, so a release can ship without the SBOM SECURITY.md promises and nothing reports it
description: release.yml:150-168 downloads the SBOM artifact and carries `continue-on-error: true` at line 168. Its `run-id` at line 164 is `${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}`, which is empty on the `release: published` trigger declared at lines 46-48, so on the path SECURITY.md:105 documents as "Manual: create + publish the release first, then push the tag" the download cannot resolve a run and fails. The failure is then invisible: the next step's `shopt -s nullglob` at line 219 makes `*.cdx.json` expand to nothing, and "Build artifact list" at lines 253-255 only appends the SBOM `if [ -f ... ]`. So a release simply comes out one asset short with a green workflow. SECURITY.md:77-83 states that every tagged release is accompanied by a CycloneDX SBOM. I verified against the live releases API that v3.5.1 through v3.7.2 all do carry one today, because the later `workflow_run` run clobbers the assets, so this is a latent silent-degradation path rather than a current break: it materialises whenever docker-publish.yml itself fails (whereupon release.yml's `if` at lines 62-64 also skips the workflow_run path entirely).
impact: A release that lost its SBOM looks identical to one that did not. The maintainer gets no signal, and a consumer verifying against SECURITY.md's list finds an asset missing with no explanation.
recommendation: Drop `continue-on-error: true` at release.yml:168 and instead set a step output, then fail the "Build artifact list" step (or write a `::warning::` plus a `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` line) when the SBOM is absent. Default `run-id` to `${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || '' }}` guarded by an `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'` so the manual path does not attempt a download it cannot satisfy.

title: sha256sums.txt is never signed, so on the documented cosign-absent path the updater's checksum check compares a tarball against a manifest fetched from the same host and adds no integrity guarantee
description: release.yml:222 writes `sha256sums.txt` and lines 230-232 sign only the source tarball (`cosign sign-blob --bundle vulnradar-${TAG}.tar.gz.cert vulnradar-${TAG}.tar.gz`). Nothing signs the sums file. lib/updater/apply.ts:87 requires `sha256sums.txt` and treats a mismatch as a hard failure, while lib/updater/cosign.ts:44-51 returns `attempted: false` and does not fail when the cosign binary is missing, with the message "the release was still checksum-verified" and the module header asserting "checksum verification still runs and is a hard gate either way". On a host without cosign (bare Node, Pterodactyl-style panels, which that same header names as the common case) both the tarball and the unsigned sums file come from the same GitHub release, so an attacker who can alter release assets alters both and the check passes.
impact: The updater's fallback integrity story is weaker than its own comments claim. Only self-hosters running the published Docker image are actually protected, because Dockerfile:59 and 84 bundle the cosign binary; everyone else gets a check that cannot detect a compromised release host or a compromised maintainer account.
recommendation: Sign `sha256sums.txt` in release.yml alongside the tarball (`cosign sign-blob --bundle sha256sums.txt.cert sha256sums.txt`), attach the bundle, and have lib/updater/apply.ts verify that bundle before trusting the sums file. Reword the header in lib/updater/cosign.ts so it no longer describes the checksum path as an integrity gate when cosign is absent.

title: CI runs a floating Node 22.x while the Dockerfile pins 22.11.0, so CI can pass on a runtime feature the published image does not have
description: .nvmrc contains `22`, package.json declares `engines.node: ">=22.0.0"`, and ci.yml passes `node-version: "22"` at lines 33, 58, 89 (via 95-98), 127 and 189, all of which resolve to whatever the newest 22.x is on the runner at job time. Dockerfile:11 and 62 pin `node:22.11.0-alpine` for both the builder and the runner stage, and release.yml:115 also uses `node-version: "22"` for the extension build. Nothing reconciles the two. This is a different axis from AUDIT-013#deps-03 (base images being stale and not covered by a dependabot docker ecosystem) and AUDIT-013#subdeps-08 (cli/ declaring `>=18`): here the same Node major is used everywhere but the minor is pinned in one place and floating in the other.
impact: A change relying on anything added after Node 22.11.0 typechecks, tests and builds green in CI and then throws at runtime inside the published image, with no CI job able to catch it. The gap is real: CI today runs a 22.x roughly a year newer than 22.11.0.
recommendation: Replace `node-version: "22"` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc` in every setup-node step in ci.yml and release.yml, and put the exact pin (`22.11.0`) in .nvmrc so CI, the Dockerfile and local development all agree. Bump all three together.

title: The dependabot auto-merge workflow's header promises patch and minor updates but the condition only ever matches patch
description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:3 states "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes" and line 4 says "Major updates (e.g. next major bump) are NOT auto-merged", implying minor is in scope. The condition at line 30 is `steps.metadata.outputs.update-type == 'version-update:semver-patch'` and nothing tests for `semver-minor`, so every minor bump sits waiting for a human despite the documented behaviour. The header also names "after CI passes" as the gate, which per ci-03 is not enforced.
impact: Minor bumps queue up unattended because a maintainer reading the header believes they are handled automatically. Combined with .github/dependabot.yml's grouped updates (where `update-type` reports the highest change in the group), most weeks' PRs fall outside the patch-only condition and no one is watching for them.
recommendation: Either extend the condition at dependabot-auto-merge.yml:30 to `(update-type == 'version-update:semver-patch' || update-type == 'version-update:semver-minor')`, or correct the header at line 3 to say patch only. Decide deliberately: minor bumps of the grouped `next-stack` and `ui` groups are exactly the ones a human should look at.

title: Releases are cosign-signed but carry no build provenance, and nothing verifies that the git tag matches the version the image reports
description: docker-publish.yml signs the image (lines 70-76) and release.yml signs the source tarball (lines 230-232), both keyless via Fulcio and Rekor. A cosign signature attests who signed, not what went into the artifact: there is no `actions/attest-build-provenance` step, no `--provenance` on the build (the build is a plain `docker build` at line 49, so buildx provenance is not produced either), and no SLSA attestation anywhere. Separately, nothing in either workflow checks that the pushed tag agrees with `package.json` (`3.7.2`) or `lib/config/config-values.ts:17` (`CONFIG_APP_VERSION = "3.7.2"`), which is the value the running container reports from app/api/version/route.ts and which the self-updater compares against the GitHub tag. A tag pushed without the matching version bump produces an image that permanently reports itself "behind" and re-offers the same update.
impact: A verifier can confirm a release was signed by this repository's Actions identity but cannot confirm which commit, workflow inputs, or base image produced the layers, which is the property SLSA provenance exists to give and the one a security product's consumers are most likely to ask for. The missing tag-versus-version check makes a mismatched release possible with no signal until self-hosters see a permanent update prompt.
recommendation: Add `actions/attest-build-provenance` after the push in docker-publish.yml (the job already has `id-token: write`) or switch to `docker/build-push-action` with `provenance: mode=max`, and attest the release tarball in release.yml the same way. Add a first step to docker-publish.yml that fails if `${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}` does not equal `node -p "require('./package.json').version"` and CONFIG_APP_VERSION.

title: The six database pool tunables are documented on /docs/config and set in the production environment but appear nowhere in .env.example
description: lib/database/db.ts:44-76 reads six pool tunables through its tunable() helper: DATABASE_POOL_MAX, DATABASE_POOL_MIN, DATABASE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and DATABASE_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS. app/docs/config/page.tsx:823-845 documents all six under 'Database pool tuning (optional)'. None of the six appears in .env.example, set or commented. Comparing key names only, the working tree's .env.local sets exactly two variables that .env.example does not have, and both are from this group (DATABASE_POOL_MAX and DATABASE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS), so the production deployment relies on tunables the shipped template does not mention. A bad value here is not silently ignored: lib/database/db.ts:49-54 throws on any non-finite or negative value.
impact: A self-hoster who copies .env.example gets no template or comment for the six knobs the docs tell them to reach for, so they either miss them or guess the spelling and hit the throw at lib/database/db.ts:49. The three-way disagreement (read by code, documented in the docs, absent from the example) is exactly the drift .env.example exists to prevent.
recommendation: Add a commented 'Database pool tuning (optional)' block to .env.example listing all six keys with their shipped defaults from CONFIG_DB_* in lib/config/config-values.ts, mirroring the wording at app/docs/config/page.tsx:823-845.

title: Two documented defaults disagree with the code, and .env.example points readers at the wrong docs page for the CONFIG_* reference
description: lib/config/config-values.ts:907-909 documents the tunable as 'CONFIG_BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 300 (5 min hard cap, matches the product promise and prevents runaway sessions)', while :913 sets it to 360 and :911-912 and :1307 both describe it correctly as 6 minutes. The stated default is 60 seconds below the shipped one, which is the same class of error AUDIT-011#drift-31 found on the API reference page for the same subsystem. Separately, .env.example:329-330 tells the reader 'See docs/setup for the full reference' for the CONFIG_* values; the CONFIG_* reference is /docs/config (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:82-85), and /docs/setup is the install guide. CLAUDE.md:118 also gives TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL as 'e.g., "310+"' where lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:8 generates "795+".
impact: Small individually, but the browserbase one is a doc-comment that sits four lines above the constant it misdescribes, so anyone tuning session length believes they are lowering a cap that is already lower than reality. The .env.example pointer sends a self-hoster to a page that does not have what they were promised.
recommendation: Fix the comment at lib/config/config-values.ts:908 to 360 (6 min) so it matches :911-913, change .env.example:330 to 'See /docs/config for the full reference', and either update the CLAUDE.md example to the current label or drop the number since it is generated.

title: Six CSS variables are defined and never read, and eight Tailwind colour utilities are wired to variables that are never defined, so bg-sidebar silently renders nothing
description: Records design-language.md A3 item 8 as an actionable finding, verified against the current tree. app/globals.css:211-213 defines --surface-1, --surface-2 and --surface-3 for the light theme and :256-258 repeats them for dark. No file in app/, components/ or lib/ reads them, and tailwind.config.mjs does not map them to a utility either, so they are unreachable by any means. Separately, tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 declares a full `sidebar` colour group (DEFAULT, foreground, primary, primary-foreground, accent, accent-foreground, border, ring) resolving to hsl(var(--sidebar-background)) and seven siblings. None of those eight variables is defined anywhere in app/globals.css or any other stylesheet, and no component uses bg-sidebar, text-sidebar-foreground or any of the group. So the utilities exist, autocomplete offers them, and each resolves to hsl() with an empty argument, which is an invalid colour the browser drops.
impact: Six dead declarations in the critical CSS. More costly is the sidebar group: a developer building the next sidebar reaches for bg-sidebar because Tailwind's IntelliSense lists it, gets a transparent element with no error in the console or the build, and has to work out why. The product already has two sidebars (/profile and /admin) that both hand-rolled bg-primary/10 instead, which is what that group was presumably added for.
recommendation: Delete --surface-1, --surface-2 and --surface-3 from both blocks in app/globals.css (:210-213 and :255-258). For the sidebar group, decide once: either delete tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 entirely, or define the eight variables in both :root and .dark and use them in the shared section-nav component proposed in dsn-10. Deleting is the smaller change and matches how the two existing sidebars are actually built; if it stays, the variables must be defined in the same commit so the utilities are never resolvable-but-empty.

title: Thirty-one routes reimplement the rate-limit message instead of using the shared helper, and the inline copies render 'Try again in 1 minute(s).'
description: lib/config/constants.ts:297-:298 defines ERROR_MESSAGES.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS(resource, minutes), which pluralizes correctly: `minute${minutes > 1 ? 's' : ''}`. Thirty-one call sites compute `Math.ceil(rl.retryAfterSeconds / 60)` themselves and build their own sentence; the distinct strings include 'Too many 2FA attempts. Try again in N minute(s).', 'Too many AI requests...', 'Too many BrowserBase sessions...', 'Too many domains added recently...', 'Too many tag changes...' (app/api/v3/scan/tags/route.ts:53), 'Too many verification attempts...' (app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:47), 'Too many requests. Please try again in N minute(s).' and 'Too many contact requests. Please try again in N minute(s).'. Every inline copy uses the literal 'minute(s)' and so prints 'Try again in 1 minute(s).' on the common single-minute case, and the set is split between 'Try again in' and 'Please try again in' for the same event. ERROR_MESSAGES is imported by zero client components (a grep for it across components/ and app/ .tsx files returns nothing), so it is a server-only table.
impact: Users see the parenthetical-plural tell on the most common rate-limit response, and the same 429 is worded three different ways depending on which endpoint they hit. Changing the wording once means editing thirty-one files.
recommendation: Route the thirty-one sites through ERROR_MESSAGES.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, extending it with an optional resource-specific noun where the current copy carries one, so the pluralization and the sentence shape live in one place.

title: ERROR_MESSAGES.WEAK_PASSWORD has no callers and states a minimum of 8 characters four lines below the constant that sets it to 12
description: lib/config/constants.ts:294 declares `WEAK_PASSWORD: 'Password must be at least 8 characters long.'`. The same file exports PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = CONFIG_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH at :255, and that value is 12 (lib/config/config-values.ts:314) and admin-editable (lib/config/registry.ts:2130). A whole-repo grep for WEAK_PASSWORD returns exactly one hit, the declaration itself, so nothing renders it today. Its live counterpart does it correctly: components/auth/reset-password-form.tsx:101 interpolates `At least ${PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH} characters` and :106 sets minLength from the same constant.
impact: No user impact today because the string is dead, but it is a loaded gun: the next route that reaches for the obvious ERROR_MESSAGES entry for a weak password ships a message that contradicts the enforced minimum, on a deployment where the operator may have raised it further.
recommendation: Either delete WEAK_PASSWORD or turn it into a function of the resolved minimum, `WEAK_PASSWORD: (min: number) => \`Password must be at least ${min} characters long.\``, matching the TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS shape three lines above it.

title: A tunables comment in config-values.ts states CONFIG_BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 300 five lines above the line that sets it to 360
description: lib/config/config-values.ts:907-:909 reads 'Tunables: CONFIG_BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 300 (5 min hard cap, matches the product promise and prevents runaway sessions).' Line 913 sets `export const CONFIG_BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 360;` and the immediately preceding comment at :911-:912 explains the 360 as 'a 60-second buffer over the 5-minute user budget'. So the file states two different values for the same constant within six lines, and the stale one is in the block an operator reads first. This is the in-file twin of AUDIT-011#drift-31, which found the published API docs stating a browser-session TTL default 60 seconds below the real value; that finding covered app/docs/api/page.tsx:525, not this comment.
impact: An operator scanning the configuration file for the session cap reads 300, sizes their Browserbase minute budget on it, and is billed against 360. It also makes the AUDIT-011#drift-31 docs fix look already done when the source of the wrong number is still in the tree.
recommendation: Update the Tunables block at lib/config/config-values.ts:908 to 360 and fold in the buffer explanation that already sits at :911, so there is one statement of the value in the file.

title: No twitter:site handle and no search-engine verification tokens are configured, and the Organization sameAs lists no social profile, so X cards are attributed to nobody
description: lib/config/config-values.ts:231 sets CONFIG_SEO_TWITTER_HANDLE to the empty string, and both lib/seo/metadata.ts:120 and app/layout.tsx:88 deliberately omit the `twitter:site` tag rather than emit an empty one (which is the right handling of an unset value). Lines 236-237 set CONFIG_SEO_GOOGLE_VERIFICATION and CONFIG_SEO_BING_VERIFICATION to empty strings, so no ownership meta tag is published either; verification may well be done by DNS instead, which is why this is low and not higher. components/seo/structured-data.tsx:75 builds `sameAs` from SEO_GITHUB_URL, DISCORD_INVITE_URL, CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL: four real, config-derived links and no social profile of any kind.
impact: An X card for any page on the site renders without the "@handle" attribution line, so a card someone reshares carries no route back to an account to follow, and X has no verified entity to associate the domain with. sameAs is what answer engines use to resolve a name to one entity, and the brief flags AI assistants not knowing this product as an existing symptom (the primary cause is the Cloudflare block, see seo-23); a sameAs with no social presence gives them less to work with.
recommendation: If an X account exists, set CONFIG_SEO_TWITTER_HANDLE in lib/config/config-values.ts:231 (with the leading @) and add the profile URL to the sameAs array in components/seo/structured-data.tsx:75 via a new CONFIG_SEO_X_URL, keeping the filter(Boolean) so a fork without one publishes nothing. Add the npm package URL to sameAs once the `vulnradar` name is claimed (see AUDIT-013#subdeps-01), plus the GitHub organisation page. Confirm Search Console and Bing ownership are established by DNS; if they are, add a one-line comment at lines 236-237 saying so, because an empty verification constant reads like an oversight.

title: Five CODEOWNERS rules match no path in the repository, including both database-migration rules, and scripts/README.md calls a script a CI gate that no workflow runs
description: .github/CODEOWNERS lists five path rules that cannot match anything in the current tree. Lines 17-19 name /app/api/v2/auth/, /app/api/v2/billing/ and /app/api/v2/webhooks/, but app/api/ contains only security-txt/, v3/ and version/: there is no v2. Lines 33-34 name /scripts/migrate.mjs and /scripts/create-fresh-db.mjs, both of which moved into subdirectories (scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs and scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs) and no longer exist at those paths. The header comment on those two calls them the 'Database migrations' owners. Separately, scripts/README.md:63 states 'The CI gate `node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs` is also part of the pre-commit checklist'; no workflow under .github/workflows/ runs any script from scripts/ (the only references to scripts/ anywhere in .github/ are the two stale CODEOWNERS lines). Duplicate check ids are in fact gated, but by a vitest case at tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts:60 ('check IDs are unique across the registry'), not by that script.
impact: Low, because the catch-all '* @dbcaa @RejectModders' on CODEOWNERS line 10 already assigns both owners to every file, so no review is actually skipped. What is lost is intent: the five specific rules were written to mark security-critical and migration paths, and a future change to line 10 (say, adding a third owner or narrowing the catch-all) would silently leave the migration runner and the auth/billing/webhook API with no explicit owner. The README's 'CI gate' wording will make someone believe a check exists where it does not.
recommendation: In .github/CODEOWNERS replace lines 17-19 with /app/api/v3/auth/, /app/api/v3/billing/ and /app/api/v3/webhooks/, and lines 33-34 with /scripts/migrate/ and /scripts/create-fresh-db/. In scripts/README.md:63 either reword to 'pre-commit checklist (see AGENTS.md); duplicate ids are gated in CI by tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts', or add a step running node scripts/find-duplicate-ids.mjs to the lint job in .github/workflows/ci.yml so the sentence becomes true.

title: The Dockerfile and package.json both document an npm allow-scripts whitelist that does not exist: .npmrc has no such setting and npm has no allowScripts field
description: Dockerfile:19-24 says: '--ignore-scripts prevents transitive postinstall scripts from running during image build. Native deps (sharp, esbuild, unrs-resolver, core-js) are whitelisted in .npmrc so they DO run via npm's `allow-scripts` mechanism.' Three parts of that are wrong. (1) The whole of .npmrc is three lines, `audit-level=high`, `fund=false`, `update-notifier=false`. There is no whitelist in it. (2) npm has no `allow-scripts` mechanism; the `allowScripts` object at package.json:156-160 is not a field npm reads (it is the key `@lavamoat/allow-scripts` uses under a `lavamoat` parent, and pnpm's equivalent is `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies`), so npm silently ignores it. (3) Two of the four packages named do not match the tree: `esbuild` is not installed at all (`npm ls esbuild` returns empty), and `sharp` 0.35.3 has `hasInstallScript: false` in the lockfile because 0.35 ships prebuilt binaries as @img/* optional dependencies rather than building at install time. Scanning every lockfile entry for `hasInstallScript`, the tree has exactly three: core-js 3.49.0 (a donation banner, reachable only through the unused jspdf, see deps-01), fsevents 2.3.3 (macOS-only, optional) and unrs-resolver 1.12.2 (dev-only, used by eslint-import-resolver-typescript, and the Docker build never lints). So `--ignore-scripts` is currently harmless, but for the opposite reason to the one the comment gives.
impact: Nothing breaks today. The hazard is the next native dependency. A maintainer who adds one, hits a broken image, and follows the comment will add a name to the `allowScripts` block at package.json:156, get no error from npm, and still ship a broken image, with the config change looking like it should have worked. The comment also misstates the security posture in the other direction: it reads as 'we ran a curated set of install scripts on purpose' when in fact none ran.
recommendation: Delete the `allowScripts` block at package.json:156-160 and rewrite the Dockerfile:19-24 comment to say what actually happens: `--ignore-scripts` is on, no install script runs during the image build, and none is needed because sharp 0.35 and the Next SWC binaries ship prebuilt. If a future dependency genuinely needs its install script, the correct fix is a targeted `npm rebuild <pkg>` line after `npm ci`, not a whitelist field.

title: docker-compose.yml pins the app image at 3.0.0 while the repo is on 3.7.2, so a self-hoster following the shipped compose file gets a two-month-old build with every audit fix since missing
description: docker-compose.yml:53 is `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0`. package.json:3 is version 3.7.2. `git log -L 53,53:docker-compose.yml` shows the tag was last touched on 2026-06-28 by commit cbc7652e ('fix(security): close 1 critical, 8 high, 11 medium findings from audit'), so the pin has not moved across seven minor releases. The pin itself is deliberate and well commented (docker-compose.yml:46-52 explains why a fixed tag beats `:latest` and how to move to a digest), but nothing in the release pipeline updates it: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml pushes `$IMAGE:${VERSION}` and `$IMAGE:latest` on a tag push (lines 53-54) and never writes back to the compose file, and there is no docker ecosystem in dependabot.yml to notice (see deps-03).
impact: The compose file is the documented self-hosting path. Anyone who clones the repo today and runs `docker compose up` gets release 3.0.0, which predates every security and correctness fix shipped in 3.1 through 3.7.2, including the remediations from AUDIT-010 through AUDIT-012. They will also be running a schema that instrumentation.ts in the checked-out repo no longer matches, since the app image carries its own copy.
recommendation: Add a step to .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml that rewrites the tag in docker-compose.yml:53 to the released version and commits it, or change the line to `ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:${VULNRADAR_VERSION:-3.7.2}` so the default tracks the repo version and a self-hoster can still pin. Either way bump it to 3.7.2 now.

title: vitest collects only .test.ts, so a .test.tsx file is silently never run, and with no DOM environment or testing-library dependency no component can be rendered in a test at all
description: vitest.config.ts:24 sets `include: ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.spec.ts"]` and line 23 sets `environment: "node"`. Neither `.test.tsx` nor `.spec.tsx` is collected, and package.json declares no jsdom, happy-dom, @testing-library/react, or @testing-library/dom dependency (grep returns nothing for all four). Counted: tests/ holds 356 `.test.ts` files, 0 `.spec.ts`, and 0 `.test.tsx`. The 8 files under tests/components/ test only extracted pure helpers (queue-status-utils, settings-registry-utils, utils, danger-score-trend), not components. The mechanical failure: a contributor adds `tests/components/scanner/scan-form.test.tsx`, runs `npm test`, gets a normal green run with no warning that their file was not collected (vitest reports nothing about files outside `include`), and ships. Even a `.test.ts` file that imported a component would fail, since `environment: "node"` supplies no document.
impact: Two effects. First, a contributor can believe they have shipped a test that has never run once, which is worse than no test. Second, none of the 266 .tsx files under components/ has any behavioural test, so hook state, conditional rendering, and event handlers are covered only by the typechecker. Given the AUDIT-011 critical finding was a UI regression (admin row actions invisible but still hit-testable on touch), that gap is the one most likely to recur.
recommendation: Add `"tests/**/*.test.tsx"` and `"tests/**/*.spec.tsx"` to `include` in vitest.config.ts:24 so a .tsx suite cannot be silently skipped. If component tests are wanted, add jsdom plus @testing-library/react as devDependencies and set `environment` per file via the `// @vitest-environment jsdom` docblock rather than switching the whole suite off node.

title: Sixty-five suites index mockQuery.mock.calls positionally while the real 30-second module-level settings cache decides whether a settings query lands in that list, so running a single test with -t can fail a test that passes in a full run
description: lib/config/runtime-config.ts:64 caches the whole system_settings snapshot at module scope for TTL_MS = 30_000. Because vitest isolates per file but not per test, the first it() in a file that reaches a settings read issues a `SELECT key, value FROM system_settings` through the mocked pool and warms the snapshot; every later it() in the same file does not. Any test that then reads `mockQuery.mock.calls[0]` or `[1]` is reading a different call depending on which test ran first. Three suites document the hazard in their own comments and defend against it: tests/app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.test.ts:30-38 ("whichever test first reaches the Promise.all in the route would warm it and silently change how many pool.query calls, and in what order, every later test makes"), tests/lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.test.ts:33-36, and tests/app/api/v3/history/route.test.ts:17-28, which intercepts the settings SQL inside the mock instead. 36 files call invalidateSettingsCache(). Counted: 65 files mock @/lib/database/db, do not mock @/lib/config/runtime-config, never call invalidateSettingsCache, never intercept the system_settings query, and do index mock.calls positionally. vitest.config.ts declares no setupFiles, so every suite has to remember this by hand.
impact: Deterministic today only because vitest runs a file's tests in declaration order. The moment a developer narrows a run with `npx vitest run <file> -t "..."`, a different test warms the cache and the positional index points at the wrong query, producing a failure that does not reproduce in a full run. The same breaks if anyone enables sequence.shuffle or reorders tests during a refactor. The debugging cost is high because the failure looks like a real assertion failure about SQL.
recommendation: Add `setupFiles: ["tests/_setup.ts"]` to the test block in vitest.config.ts and have that file call `invalidateSettingsCache()` in a global beforeEach, so the snapshot is cold for every test in every suite. That removes the hazard for all 191 DB-mocking suites at once and lets the three hand-written guards be deleted.

title: The server config module lands in the root-layout client chunk, carrying dead process.env.SMTP_PASS and BROWSERBASE_API_KEY reads into every page's JavaScript
description: lib/config/constants.ts (787 lines) re-exports lib/config/config-values.ts (1,367 lines) and is imported directly by client components across the app, including ones mounted in app/layout.tsx. The compiled result is visible in the committed build: static/chunks/9711-3989d97c24edd68e.js, 18 KB and part of the /layout entry (so present on all 311 routes), contains `i.env.SMTP_HOST, i.env.SMTP_PORT, i.env.SMTP_USER, i.env.SMTP_PASS, i.env.SMTP_FROM||i.env.SMTP_USER;` and `i.env.BROWSERBASE_API_KEY&&i.env.BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID;` as bare expression statements alongside the team-role matrix and the API route table. No secret is disclosed: `i` is Next's client process shim and only NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables are inlined, so these evaluate to undefined -- but the code and the variable names ship, and every unused constant webpack cannot prove dead ships with them.
impact: Every page in the app carries a slice of the server configuration module and dead environment reads for SMTP credentials and the Browserbase API key. It is bytes and noise today, and it is one careless `NEXT_PUBLIC_` rename away from becoming a real disclosure, since the read sites are already compiled into a client chunk.
recommendation: Enforce the split the project already documents in CLAUDE.md: keep lib/config/client-constants.ts as the only module client components import, move the process.env-reading blocks (EMAIL_CONFIG and the Browserbase configured check in lib/config/constants.ts) into a server-only module marked with `import "server-only"`, and change the client-side imports of @/lib/config/constants over to the client-safe module.

title: Dead configuration objects and constants, including a FEATURES object where seven of eight members are unread
description: The FEATURES object at lib/config/constants.ts:778-786 has exactly one live member: a grep for FEATURES.[A-Z_]+ outside lib/config returns one hit, lib/hooks/use-client-config.ts:33 reading .PDF_REPORTS. The other seven (DEMO_MODE, TEAMS, API_KEYS, WEBHOOKS, SCHEDULED_SCANS, BULK_SCANS, EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS) are read nowhere; the underlying CONFIG_FEATURE_* values are alive via the registry, so only this convenience object is dead. Also dead: the DATABASE object (:478-484, no matches for DATABASE.[A-Z_]), PATTERNS (:338), PAGINATION (:500), ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (:641), AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE (:242), API_KEY_SCOPE_DESCRIPTIONS (client-constants.ts:346), CONFIG_API_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS (config-values.ts:660), CONFIG_FOOTER_TEXT (:191), HISTORY_REPORT (client-constants.ts:151, zero web callers - the export menu regenerates all five formats client-side, and only the extension uses the route). Catalog helpers getFreePlan (catalog.ts:305), isPaidPlan (:309) and getApiLimitForPlan (:318) have tests as their only callers. Five unused skeleton exports at components/admin/shared/skeleton.tsx:18,40,62,90,114 (about 110 lines). components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:9-11 documents a width="wide" prop no caller uses - see auth-11, which is the screen it was written for. lib/config/public-paths.ts:66 lists ROUTES.GDPR_REQUEST as "/legal/privacy#gdpr" but middleware.ts:265 matches on pathname, which never contains a fragment, so the entry can never match (harmless, line 49 covers it).
impact: Cleanup only, but the HISTORY_REPORT case has a real consequence: the server route additionally runs attachRemediation (app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:149-155), so extension-exported reports and web-exported reports are not byte-identical.
recommendation: Deletions need owner sign-off. The one to act on regardless is the report divergence: decide whether the extension and the web app should produce the same file, and make them agree.

title: Two parsed environment variables are never consulted, one of them documented
description: CONTACT_EMAIL is parsed at lib/config/env.ts:85 and appears in .env.example and the docs, but the contact route sends to NOREPLY_EMAIL (app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:146). STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is parsed at :60 while only the NEXT_PUBLIC_ variant is ever read.
impact: A self-hoster sets CONTACT_EMAIL as documented and contact mail goes elsewhere.
recommendation: Either honour CONTACT_EMAIL in the contact route or remove it from env.ts, .env.example and the docs. Remove the unused STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY parse.

title: The opt-in screenshot wait is capped at 30 seconds, longer than the entire rest of the scan
description: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:812 awaits the screenshot with CONFIG_SCAN_SCREENSHOT_MAX_WAIT_MS = 30_000 (lib/config/config-values.ts:1013).
impact: Only affects users who tick the box, but when it bites it more than doubles the wait.
recommendation: Reduce the cap, or render results first and let the screenshot populate asynchronously.

title: CSP connect-src has trailing https: wss: wildcards
description: CSP connect-src 'self' https://challenges.cloudflare.com ... https://www.browserbase.com wss://*.browserbase.com https: wss: ends with the scheme-only wildcards https: wss:, which permits fetch/XHR/WS to any HTTPS origin.
recommendation: Drop the trailing 'https:' 'wss:' scheme wildcards; allowlist specific API hosts.

title: Negative result for the next audit: the four config surfaces share no duplicated export, all 271 registry defaults derive from CONFIG_ constants, and all seven paginated routes use the same page/limit convention
description:
I checked the specific split-brain shape AUDIT-009#dup-01 found (RATE_LIMITS defined in two places so 11 routes bypassed the admin-configured values) against the current tree and it has not recurred.

Extracting every `export const` and `export function` from lib/config/constants.ts (788 lines), lib/config/client-constants.ts (378), lib/config/config-values.ts (1,368), lib/config/registry.ts, lib/config/brand.ts and lib/config/env.ts gives zero names exported from more than one of them. The layering holds in the direction it is documented: config-values.ts holds the literals, constants.ts imports and re-exports them (RATE_LIMITS at constants.ts:360-470 is built entirely from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_* imports, with no second literal anywhere), and client-constants.ts is re-exported through constants.ts rather than redefined.

lib/config/registry.ts contains 272 `default:` entries and every one of them is a CONFIG_ constant imported from config-values.ts, not a literal, so an admin-editable setting cannot fall back to a value that disagrees with the compiled one. The comment at registry.ts:1-11 describes that rule and the code follows it.

Separately, every paginated endpoint uses the same query convention: `page` and `limit` in all seven (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts, admin/content, admin/email-logs, admin/error-logs, admin/teams, ai/conversations, public-scans). Nothing uses offset or a cursor. The response-side key drift is filed as dup-08; the request side is consistent.

The brand palette is likewise consolidated: lib/config/brand.ts is the single source and lib/email/email.ts:19-47 aliases it rather than holding its own hexes, which is what the comment at brand.ts:1-13 claims.
impact: None. Recorded so the next audit does not spend time re-deriving these four surfaces or re-checking pagination conventions.
recommendation: No action. Keep the registry.ts:1-11 rule ("Adding a configurable value means adding an entry here, not a bare constant") enforced in review; it is the thing preventing the AUDIT-009 shape from returning.

title: Several compiled config constants orphaned after their routes migrated to admin-configurable settings this session
description: AUTH_SESSION_MAX_AGE, DEVICE_TRUST_MAX_AGE, DEFAULT_API_KEY_DAILY_LIMIT, and the PAGINATION constant object all have zero remaining importers after their call sites correctly migrated to getSetting()-based values this session. Not wrong today, but a future caller grepping for these could grab the frozen constant instead of the live setting with no compiler error to catch it.
recommendation: Delete the orphaned constants now that nothing consumes them, or mark them clearly as legacy-default-only.

title: AUTH_SECRET not set in .env.local
description: AUTH_SECRET is optional. On the deployed sandbox the fallback to API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is in use. If that key is ever rotated, OAuth state tokens issued under the previous HMAC key silently fail to verify.
recommendation: Generate and set AUTH_SECRET in .env.local; document it as a separate 32+ char secret.
